newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania says revenue collection improved.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania says revenue collection improved.

text.p: Lithuania's revenue collection is improving but still falling short of its target, the parliamentary budget committee said on Thursday.

"Revenue collection has improved as it is now falling short of the target on average by one to 1.5 million litas a day against last January's shortfall of an average of three to five million litas every day," budget committee head Elvyra Kuneviciene told reporters.
She said stricter revenue collection measures implemented by the new right-wing administration were showing their first results.
The new parliament, dominated by the Homeland Union Party which won a landslide victory over a party of ex-Communists in November, approved a 1997 budget with a 697 million litas deficit.
The central government deficit is financed through the government Treasury bill market.
The previous government also managed its debt through syndicated loans and the issue of Eurobonds.
The major revenue sources of the Lithuanian budget are Value Added Tax (VAT) and excise duties.
